title: He does not need your prayer, and still He invites you
subtitle: The Rich beyond measure, and why every good deed is a gift to yourself
intro: Al-Ghaniyy (الْغَنِيُّ) means the Rich, the Free of need: Allah depends on no one and nothing, while everything depends on Him. It matters to you because it removes the pride from your worship and the fear from your poverty: you give Him nothing He lacks, and He gives you everything you lack.

root.sense: In everyday Arabic ghani means rich, but the root sense is to be free of need. A rich man is called ghani not because he owns much, but because he does not have to ask anyone: he has his own car, so he borrows no one's. Ghina is independence, sufficiency, having no lack.

row.title: He needs nothing
sub: your worship adds nothing to Him

row.title: He is doing me the favour
sub: He brought me to worship at all

knowing: Al-Ghaniyy is absolutely free of need. He did not create out of loneliness or for help; He loses nothing when people turn away and gains nothing when they worship. In a hadith qudsi in Sahih Muslim, He says that if all of creation, from the first to the last, had the heart of the most pious man, it would add nothing to His kingdom, and if all were as wicked as the worst, it would take nothing away. And if every one of them asked and He gave each his request, it would no more diminish His treasure than a needle dipped in the sea.

The flip side is stated directly: O people, you are the ones in need of Allah, and Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy (35:15). {idea}His richness and your poverty are two halves of one truth{/idea}. Notice the name He pairs it with, again and again: Al-Hamid, the Praiseworthy. Many rich people are stingy; He is rich and generous, needing no praise yet worthy of all of it.
As-Samad, a near name, highlights creation turning to Him with its needs. Al-Ghaniyy highlights His own fullness, and what that means for how you see your deeds.
seeing: Again and again the Quran says it plainly: if you disbelieve, Allah is free of need of you, yet He does not approve disbelief for His servants, and if you are grateful He is pleased with you (39:7). Musa told his people that even if they and everyone on earth disbelieved, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy (14:8). Whoever is grateful, Luqman was taught, is grateful for his own benefit (31:12).

When some Bedouins told the Prophet ﷺ that they had done him a favour by accepting Islam, the Quran answered that it was Allah who had done them a favour by guiding them. And He warns: if you turn away, He will replace you with another people who will not be like you (47:38).
trusting: Imagine visiting a billionaire's palace with a cheap bottle of perfume as a gift. You would feel embarrassed, aware that it means nothing to him. {trap}Yet we often stand in prayer feeling we have done something great, as if Allah owes us{/trap}. Al-Ghaniyy cures that. Your prayer, fasting and charity are deposits into your own account. He needs none of it.

Picture a man who borrows a jacket from one friend, trousers from another, a shirt and a belt from two more, and arrives at a wedding where everyone compliments his outfit. He cannot take the credit; none of it is his. {reward}That is how you look at your talent, your wealth and even your worship once you know Al-Ghaniyy{/reward}: all of it borrowed, all of it His gift. Pride falls away, and gratitude takes its place.

And when you are short of money, His richness is your hope. The Prophet ﷺ said, as reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, that true richness is not having many possessions but richness of the soul. Ask the Rich for what you need, and ask Him for a content heart.
loving: It is one thing to be loved by someone who needs you. It is another to be loved by Someone who needs nothing at all. {idea}Al-Ghaniyy chose to create you, guide you and invite you, while gaining nothing from it{/idea}. Every blessing He gives is pure generosity, with no hidden interest. That is the kind of love that melts pride and makes the heart fall down in thanks.
now: Someone at the mosque praises your recitation, or a colleague says your charity drive was amazing, and you feel a warm glow of pride. Before it settles, say inwardly: this was never mine. Al-Ghaniyy lent me the voice, the money and the will. Then thank Him, not yourself.
old: I work hard at my religion, so I feel I have earned something from Allah.
new: Al-Ghaniyy needs nothing from me; every good I do is His gift, and every reward is His generosity.
try: Give something today that you actually value, not leftovers, quietly and for His sake alone (2:267).

dua.text: Ya Ghaniyy, You need nothing and I need You in everything. Enrich me with what is lawful, make my soul content, and never let me think my deeds are a favour to You.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name in times of poverty or debt, and whenever you catch yourself feeling proud of your worship.

pairs.why: The Quran often pairs them: He needs no praise, yet He is worthy of all praise, rich and generous at once.
Al-Ghaniyy is rich in Himself; Al-Mughni makes others rich. His fullness overflows to His creation.
Al-Ghaniyy needs nothing; As-Samad is the One everyone needs and turns to.

faq.a: Al-Ghaniyy means the Rich, the Free of need: Allah needs nothing and no one, while everything depends on Him. The root sense is independence rather than wealth alone. It appears in many verses, often paired with Al-Hamid, the Praiseworthy, as in 35:15.

faq.q: If Allah does not need our worship, why worship Him?
faq.a: Because we need it. The Quran says whoever is grateful is grateful for his own benefit (31:12), and whoever withholds only withholds from himself (47:38). Worship is how a needy creature receives guidance, peace and reward from the One who has everything.

faq.q: Why is Al-Ghaniyy paired with Al-Hamid?
faq.a: Al-Ghaniyy shows that Allah needs nothing, and Al-Hamid shows that He is still worthy of all praise. Some who are rich are stingy and deserve no praise; Allah is both free of need and endlessly generous, which is why the two names so often come together.
